affaan-m/ecc.pitch: An agent harness tuned for performance
affaan-m/ecc.aud: Teams that care about harness throughput and observability
affaan-m/ecc.note: Bundles skills, memory, security and a dev workflow into one optimized runtime; plenty of concepts, so read the docs.

langchain-ai/langchain.pitch: The de facto foundation for LLM application development
langchain-ai/langchain.aud: Teams that need a huge third-party integration surface
langchain-ai/langchain.note: The biggest ecosystem and the fastest release cadence, at the cost of thick abstractions and frequent breaking changes — don't expect a year without edits.

microsoft/autogen.pitch: The elder statesman of multi-agent conversations
microsoft/autogen.note: Rewritten around an event-driven actor core since v0.4; the repo is archived and development moved to microsoft/agent-framework.

crewaiinc/crewai.aud: Anyone who wants an AI team up and running fast
crewaiinc/crewai.note: Closest to how human teams split work and the quickest to start; complex state flow is less flexible than LangGraph.

run-llama/llama_index.pitch: An agent framework centered on data and RAG
run-llama/llama_index.note: Indexing and retrieval are the core strength, and event-driven workflows are now covered too.

langchain-ai/langgraph.pitch: Graph-based orchestration for stateful, resumable agents
langchain-ai/langgraph.aud: Long-running flows with human approval or resume-after-crash
langchain-ai/langgraph.note: LangChain's recommended agent track: a clear state-machine model with a medium-to-steep learning curve.

agno-agi/agno.pitch: A lightweight, high-performance multimodal agent framework
agno-agi/agno.note: Formerly phidata; ships memory, knowledge, tools and multimodal support, and feels light both in benchmarks and in practice.

langchain-ai/deepagents.pitch: LangChain's batteries-included harness for long tasks
langchain-ai/deepagents.aud: Apps that need planning, file access and sub-agents
langchain-ai/deepagents.note: Built-in planning, filesystem and sub-agents; a higher abstraction than LangGraph, so check default behavior and tool permissions first.

openai/openai-agents-python.aud: Projects on OpenAI models that need handoffs, guardrails and tracing
openai/openai-agents-python.note: Handoffs, guardrails and tracing work out of the box; model-agnostic, but best tuned for OpenAI models.

huggingface/smolagents.pitch: A code agent with a tiny core
huggingface/smolagents.aud: People who want to understand how agents work inside
huggingface/smolagents.note: The docs claim roughly a thousand lines of core, with Python code as the action space — ideal for dissection.

mastra-ai/mastra.pitch: TypeScript-native agents with workflows, RAG and eval in one package
mastra-ai/mastra.aud: Teams shipping a product in TypeScript
mastra-ai/mastra.note: From the Gatsby team: agent, workflow and eval in a single package — a rare complete option in the JS ecosystem.

microsoft/semantic-kernel.pitch: Microsoft's enterprise SDK for .NET, Python and Java
microsoft/semantic-kernel.note: The smoothest path into Azure and AI Foundry; a pure-Python team will find it heavy.

deepset-ai/haystack.pitch: Production-grade pipeline orchestration for RAG and agents
deepset-ai/haystack.aud: Enterprise search with strictly controlled retrieval chains
deepset-ai/haystack.note: Pipelines are more explicit than LangChain and easier to debug; the community is smaller.

google/adk-python.note: Ships A2A support and a deployment toolchain, so the cloud path is complete.

pydantic/pydantic-ai.aud: Heavy Python typing with maintainability first
pydantic/pydantic-ai.note: From the Pydantic team: the most solid structured-output and dependency-injection story, with a strong engineering feel.

qwenlm/qwen-agent.pitch: Alibaba's official framework for Qwen models
qwenlm/qwen-agent.note: Function calling, code interpreter, RAG and MCP all have ready implementations, tightly matched to Qwen.

voltagent/voltagent.pitch: A TypeScript agent platform with a visual debugger
voltagent/voltagent.aud: TS teams that want traces on day one
voltagent/voltagent.note: Framework plus console in one: run it and you can watch every execution trace; the ecosystem is a notch smaller than Mastra's.

strands-agents/harness-sdk.aud: Teams putting agents into production on AWS
strands-agents/harness-sdk.note: Python and TypeScript, built on the idea that the model picks the tools; Bedrock integration is a bonus.

anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.pitch: Embed Claude Code's tool loop in your own application
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.aud: Developers integrating Claude Code capabilities in Python
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.note: The official Python SDK with an agent loop, tools and permission control; not a multi-model framework — it depends on the Claude ecosystem.

cloudflare/agents.note: Built on Durable Objects, so agents are long-lived and billed by usage; meaningless outside Cloudflare.

modelscope/ms-agent.aud: Agents in the Chinese model ecosystem
modelscope/ms-agent.note: Runnable examples for code generation, deep research and agentic RL, close to the ModelScope model hub; docs and community are mostly Chinese.

n8n-io/n8n.pitch: Node-based automation with built-in AI agent nodes
n8n-io/n8n.aud: Teams with many integrations wiring business processes
n8n-io/n8n.note: An automation platform that grew agent features and connects 400+ services — better at getting work done than a pure agent framework.

langgenius/dify.pitch: Visual LLM app building plus self-hosting
langgenius/dify.aud: Teams that need an internal AI app live fast
langgenius/dify.note: The most balanced open-source platform: workflows, knowledge base, agents and observability, with friendly Chinese docs.

langflow-ai/langflow.pitch: Visual orchestration with one-click export to API or MCP
langflow-ai/langflow.aud: Taking a low-code prototype to a production endpoint
langflow-ai/langflow.note: Export it and use it as a service; the front end feels more modern than Flowise.

flowiseai/flowise.note: The lowest entry barrier, but complex logic hits the visual ceiling quickly; the repo is archived.

simstudioai/sim.pitch: A collaborative canvas for agent workflows
simstudioai/sim.aud: Drag, deploy and monitor in one place
simstudioai/sim.note: Visual orchestration that deploys and monitors directly — more product-shaped than Langflow; Apache-2.0 and clean.

activepieces/activepieces.pitch: A self-hosted open-source Zapier with AI
activepieces/activepieces.aud: Budget-sensitive automation that must stay on-prem
activepieces/activepieces.note: Positioned as iPaaS, with agents as one piece of the puzzle.

coze-dev/coze-studio.pitch: ByteDance's open-source Coze: visual agents and apps
coze-dev/coze-studio.aud: Teams that want to self-host a low-code agent platform
coze-dev/coze-studio.note: Plugins, workflows, knowledge base and publishing channels are all present — the most complete Chinese option; many components, so Docker orchestration takes patience.

morluto/rea.pitch: Reverse engineering with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries
morluto/rea.note: The most-starred repo on the list (476k): a narrow niche with surprising heat; check the compliance boundary before applying it in real work.

deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.pitch: DeepSeek's agent harness where everything is a plugin
deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.aud: Advanced users who want to customize the workflow deeply
deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.note: The official harness makes tools, skills and memory fully pluggable; it moves fast, and the docs lag behind the code.

anomalyco/opencode.pitch: The hottest open-source terminal coding agent
anomalyco/opencode.note: MIT licensed and model-provider agnostic, so you can swap freely; more stars than most closed competitors, at the cost of a fast-changing interface.

anthropics/claude-code.aud: Daily coding, refactoring and test runs
anthropics/claude-code.note: This repo mainly hosts docs and issues; closed-source distribution, but currently the strongest overall experience.

farion1231/cc-switch.pitch: One desktop panel to rule every terminal coding agent
farion1231/cc-switch.aud: People running several CLI agents at once
farion1231/cc-switch.note: A single entry point for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness accounts and sessions; it writes no code itself — it is the switchboard.

openai/codex.aud: Developers already on a ChatGPT plan
openai/codex.note: Written in Rust, with solid sandboxing and approval flows and the tightest integration with GPT models.

stablyai/orca.pitch: Run a fleet of coding agents on your own subscriptions
stablyai/orca.aud: Teams that want several coding agents in parallel
stablyai/orca.note: Reuses your existing CLI subscriptions and spreads tasks across a fleet of bots; scheduling is strong, while per-task quality depends on the agent underneath.

google-gemini/gemini-cli.pitch: Google's terminal agent with a generous free tier
google-gemini/gemini-cli.note: The million-token context is the advantage — good for reading large repos.

openhands/openhands.pitch: An open-source software engineering agent that finishes dev tasks on its own
openhands/openhands.aud: People who want an open-source Claude Code alternative
openhands/openhands.note: Works inside a sandbox to patch repos, run commands and tests; one of the strongest open-source entries on SWE-bench-style tasks.

cline/cline.pitch: An autonomous coding agent inside VS Code that reads files and runs commands
cline/cline.aud: VS Code users who want to approve every step visually
cline/cline.note: A plugin with wide adoption, flexible with any provider's API key.

aaif-goose/goose.aud: Automation that runs on your own machine
aaif-goose/goose.note: Open-sourced by Block with a mature extension model; leans toward local automation rather than pure coding.

antonosika/gpt-engineer.pitch: Generate an entire codebase from natural language
antonosika/gpt-engineer.aud: Fast scaffolding and understanding code-generation ideas
antonosika/gpt-engineer.note: An early star whose ideas traveled far; iteration has slowed.

aider-ai/aider.pitch: Git-native pair programming in the terminal
aider-ai/aider.aud: Senior developers who live in a shell
aider-ai/aider.note: Every edit becomes a commit you can roll back, and models swap freely; steady.

continuedev/continue.pitch: A customizable in-IDE assistant with an agent mode
continuedev/continue.aud: Teams connecting their own or on-prem models
continuedev/continue.note: The most flexible custom-model and context-provider setup — a good fit for intranets.

qwenlm/qwen-code.aud: Teams running terminal agents on domestic models
qwenlm/qwen-code.note: Forked from Gemini CLI and retuned; Qwen models offer generous context and it is friendly to networks in China.

charmbracelet/crush.pitch: A terminal coding agent in Go with the best TUI feel
charmbracelet/crush.aud: People who like lightweight single-binary TUIs
charmbracelet/crush.note: From the Charm team, carrying the bubbletea aesthetic; a small plugin ecosystem, but the experience wins.

eyaltoledano/claude-task-master.pitch: A task breakdown system for Cursor and Claude Code
eyaltoledano/claude-task-master.aud: Long requirements handled inside the IDE
eyaltoledano/claude-task-master.note: Turns a PRD into a task DAG and hands it to a coding agent item by item; updates have slowed over the past six months, so watch version compatibility.

kilo-org/kilocode.pitch: An all-in-one agentic engineering platform in VS Code
kilo-org/kilocode.aud: IDE users who want orchestration plus plan mode
kilo-org/kilocode.note: A beefed-up Cline lineage with orchestration and plan mode; more enterprise-flavored since the Anaconda acquisition.

roocodeinc/roo-code.pitch: A Cline fork that switches modes for architecture, coding and debugging
roocodeinc/roo-code.note: Multiple modes give different tasks different system prompts; the repo is archived.

swe-agent/swe-agent.pitch: The academic reference implementation of a software engineering agent
swe-agent/swe-agent.note: Where the Agent-Computer Interface idea came from; productization was never the goal.

swe-agent/mini-swe-agent.pitch: A minimal coding agent in 100 lines
swe-agent/mini-swe-agent.aud: People who want to read the loop and actually get it
swe-agent/mini-swe-agent.note: The SWE-agent team points newcomers here first; it runs SWE-bench and the source takes an afternoon to read.

openclaw/openclaw.pitch: A personal agent runtime that calls itself 'the AI that actually does the work'
openclaw/openclaw.aud: Anyone wanting a cross-platform always-on personal agent
openclaw/openclaw.note: Second most-starred overall (395k): a local-first gateway with 20+ messaging channels; head-to-head with Hermes, and the ecosystem is racing.

nousresearch/hermes-agent.pitch: An autonomous agent that grows its own skills and remembers you across sessions
nousresearch/hermes-agent.aud: Agents that live in a terminal or IM and work over time
nousresearch/hermes-agent.note: Accumulates and iterates skills, with persistent memory, sub-agents and cron; top of the heat chart, but the open-issue backlog is large.

significant-gravitas/autogpt.pitch: The project that set off the autonomous agent wave
significant-gravitas/autogpt.aud: Understanding agent history and prototyping automation
significant-gravitas/autogpt.note: Now repositioned as an agent-building platform; historically enormous star count, but real usage is below its peak.

foundationagents/openmanus.pitch: An open-source general agent (a Manus replica)
foundationagents/openmanus.aud: Building your own general task agent
foundationagents/openmanus.note: High community heat and fast iteration; engineering completeness is still catching up — good for tinkering, not for delivery.

hkuds/nanobot.pitch: A lightweight personal agent that works once installed
hkuds/nanobot.aud: Keeping a small always-on agent on your own machine
hkuds/nanobot.note: From HKUDS: small but complete, with tools, memory and scheduled tasks; engineering maturity still trails Hermes.

reworkd/agentgpt.pitch: Set a goal in the browser and watch it decompose and run
reworkd/agentgpt.note: An old teaching project; archived and no longer updated, kept as a teaching reference.

fosowl/agenticseek.note: Local models only and privacy first; the ceiling is your local model, so don't compare it with cloud flagships.

agent0ai/agent-zero.pitch: A general agent with a web UI, a terminal and memory
agent0ai/agent-zero.aud: Seeing an agent that 'uses a computer' out of the box
agent0ai/agent-zero.note: Clear architecture and very playable; production use needs your own isolation and permission model.

openbmb/pilotdeck.note: Isolates context and memory per WorkSpace and is positioned as a productivity platform; AGPL-3.0, so read the terms before commercial use.

ruvnet/ruflo.pitch: A veteran harness for multi-agent swarms
ruvnet/ruflo.note: Calls itself the original agent harness, with many topology options; the community debates whether it is a toy or a production tool — load-test it yourself first.

foundationagents/metagpt.pitch: Turn one sentence into a software company with roles
foundationagents/metagpt.aud: Research on multi-agent collaboration and prototype generation
foundationagents/metagpt.note: From a Chinese team; its SOP-style collaboration influenced many later projects.

agentscope-ai/agentscope.note: Emphasizes message passing and fault tolerance with friendly Chinese docs; originally designed for large-scale multi-agent simulation.

openbmb/chatdev.pitch: A virtual software company with multiple roles
openbmb/chatdev.note: The paper's companion implementation; results depend on the model, and engineering polish is average.

camel-ai/camel.pitch: Multi-agent social simulation and synthetic data generation
camel-ai/camel.aud: Research and generating agent training data
camel-ai/camel.note: Academic and highly abstracted — not meant for shipping business products.

ag2ai/ag2.pitch: An AgentOS forked from the AutoGen community
ag2ai/ag2.aud: Existing AutoGen users who want the community edition
ag2ai/ag2.note: The community took over after Microsoft moved to Agent Framework; migrating existing AutoGen projects needs the official migration guide.

browser-use/browser-use.pitch: Let an agent drive a browser like a person
browser-use/browser-use.aud: Web flow automation, scraping and form filling
browser-use/browser-use.note: The lowest-integration-cost browser agent library, compatible with the Playwright ecosystem.

microsoft/playwright-mcp.pitch: Standard browser hands and feet for agents (MCP)
microsoft/playwright-mcp.aud: Existing agents that need browser capability
microsoft/playwright-mcp.note: Officially maintained and stable, native to MCP clients.

browserbase/stagehand.pitch: Turn web pages into programmable APIs for agents
browserbase/stagehand.aud: Front-end teams doing repeatable web automation
browserbase/stagehand.note: Adds natural-language actions and caching on top of Playwright, far more stable on repeat runs than pure LLM approaches.

skyvern-ai/skyvern.pitch: Browser workflow automation with vision plus LLMs
skyvern-ai/skyvern.aud: Replacing enterprise RPA and batch form flows
skyvern-ai/skyvern.note: A near-product service with a UI that is more robust to page redesigns than selector-based tools.

nanobrowser/nanobrowser.pitch: A multi-agent browser assistant inside a Chrome extension
nanobrowser/nanobrowser.aud: Cases where you don't want to deploy a service
nanobrowser/nanobrowser.note: Runs entirely in the front end with your own key; light to try, capabilities limited by the extension sandbox.

steel-dev/steel-browser.pitch: A self-hostable browser API built for agents
steel-dev/steel-browser.aud: Teams that won't hand browser sessions to a cloud service
steel-dev/steel-browser.note: Sessions, proxies, file uploads and fingerprinting are all wrapped, so one container is enough; the real cost is operating your own Chrome cluster.

openinterpreter/openinterpreter.pitch: Natural language driving local code execution and operations
openinterpreter/openinterpreter.aud: Local batch jobs, file and data processing
openinterpreter/openinterpreter.note: Enormous privileges — use it in a controlled environment; the project's pace has slowed.

bytedance/ui-tars-desktop.pitch: ByteDance's GUI agent that looks at the screen and clicks
bytedance/ui-tars-desktop.aud: Desktop app automation and cross-app flows
bytedance/ui-tars-desktop.note: A pure-vision approach that doesn't need the DOM, so it generalizes further than browser-only tools; the repo is archived, kept for reference.

microsoft/omniparser.pitch: A visual parser that turns screenshots into clickable elements
microsoft/omniparser.aud: Building your own GUI agent that needs screen understanding
microsoft/omniparser.note: A building block for the pure-vision route, usually paired with a VLM; it isn't an agent — it gives agents eyes.

web-infra-dev/midscene.aud: Front-end teams doing E2E and AI automation
web-infra-dev/midscene.note: From a Chinese team with good Chinese docs, tightly integrated with Playwright and Puppeteer.

simular-ai/agent-s.pitch: An open-source SOTA implementation of a computer-use agent
simular-ai/agent-s.aud: Researching the ceiling of computer-use agents
simular-ai/agent-s.note: The paper's companion code, with benchmark results among the best in open source; getting it running means wiring models and environments.

microsoft/magentic-ui.pitch: A human-in-the-loop 'browser plus local files' agent
microsoft/magentic-ui.note: From Microsoft Research (MagenticLite), built so every step can be taken over and corrected; a research prototype rather than a production tool.

pipecat-ai/pipecat.pitch: A pipeline framework for real-time voice agents
pipecat-ai/pipecat.note: Chains STT, LLM and TTS into a real-time pipeline with controllable latency; you bring the models.

livekit/agents.aud: Teams that already have a LiveKit audio/video stack
livekit/agents.note: A solid WebRTC foundation with mature interruption and echo handling; less valuable outside the LiveKit ecosystem.

ten-framework/ten-framework.pitch: A real-time multimodal conversation framework (formerly TEN Agent)
ten-framework/ten-framework.note: Orchestrates audio streams, vision, LLM and TTS as one graph, focused on real-time interruption; Apache-2.0 with additional terms — read the LICENSE before commercial use.

panniantong/agent-reach.pitch: Give agents eyes on the whole internet
panniantong/agent-reach.note: A unified read and search interface for Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub and Bilibili; source availability moves with platform policy.

bytedance/deer-flow.pitch: ByteDance's deep research framework with human-in-the-loop
bytedance/deer-flow.note: Pluggable search, crawling and report modules with decent coverage of Chinese-language scenarios.

stanford-oval/storm.pitch: Generate sourced long-form writing like a Wikipedia article
stanford-oval/storm.note: From Stanford: outline first, then retrieve section by section, with strong structure.

assafelovic/gpt-researcher.note: Quick to start with usable output; depth depends heavily on the model and the search sources.

microsoft/rd-agent.note: Closes the loop of hypothesis, code, experiment and review, aimed at data science; the integration cost is high.

langchain-ai/open_deep_research.aud: Building a research agent of your own
langchain-ai/open_deep_research.note: Built on LangGraph with a clear, hackable structure; the repo is archived, kept as a structural reference.

graphify-labs/graphify.pitch: Turn an entire codebase into a queryable knowledge graph
graphify-labs/graphify.note: Graphs code, docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs together, with an agent-facing query interface; large repos take a while to graph.

infiniflow/ragflow.pitch: A RAG engine built for deep document understanding
infiniflow/ragflow.note: Table and scanned-document parsing is the strength; ships a UI and has many deployments in China.

mintplex-labs/anything-llm.pitch: A ready-to-run private ChatGPT with a document library
mintplex-labs/anything-llm.aud: Individuals and small teams building a knowledge assistant
mintplex-labs/anything-llm.note: Deploys in about ten minutes; sufficient and restrained — don't expect complex orchestration.

hkuds/lightrag.aud: Graph-style retrieval without a heavyweight stack
hkuds/lightrag.note: Uses graph structure to cover the relational blind spot of vector search, at lower cost than GraphRAG.

khoj-ai/khoj.aud: Building your own personal knowledge assistant
khoj-ai/khoj.note: Documents, email and web pages all flow in, with local model support; no commits in months, so the pace has dropped.

tencent/weknora.pitch: Tencent's open-source document understanding and retrieval platform
tencent/weknora.aud: Turning a pile of PDFs and Word files into a Q&A knowledge base
tencent/weknora.note: A complete chain from parsing to chunking to multi-path recall to cited answers — a Go service, not a toy. MIT, but third-party components carry their own terms.

microsoft/graphrag.aud: Global questions and cross-document relationship reasoning
microsoft/graphrag.note: Graph construction is expensive in tokens; suited to high-value corpora.

onyx-dot-app/onyx.pitch: An enterprise knowledge Q&A platform (formerly Danswer)
onyx-dot-app/onyx.note: Many connectors and a complete permission model, good for internal deployment; the component stack is heavy.

mem0ai/mem0.pitch: A long-term memory layer you bolt onto an agent
mem0ai/mem0.note: Both hosted and self-hosted, and the most widely deployed memory layer.

mempalace/mempalace.pitch: A memory system that claims the best benchmark scores
mempalace/mempalace.note: Leads with benchmarks and offers several backends; 'best-benchmarked' is self-reported — reproduce it before trusting it.

topoteretes/cognee.pitch: Turn documents into graph memory for agents
topoteretes/cognee.note: ETL-style graph building with memory you can query and edit; engineering-heavy, with quite a few settings.

getzep/graphiti.pitch: A real-time knowledge graph for agents with a timeline
getzep/graphiti.aud: Memory that needs to know who changed what, and when
getzep/graphiti.note: Zep's memory engine: entity relations plus temporal validity, so it can answer 'is this still true?' rather than only 'what was said'. Graphiti is the engine, Zep the hosted service.

supermemoryai/supermemory.pitch: A high-speed memory and context engine with a hosted API
supermemoryai/supermemory.aud: Product teams that want a memory API now
supermemoryai/supermemory.note: Delivered as a service, so integration is easy; the self-hosted version trails the SaaS one.

letta-ai/letta.pitch: A stateful agent service that manages its own memory (formerly MemGPT)
letta-ai/letta.aud: Agents that need a long-term persona and memory
letta-ai/letta.note: Treats memory like an operating system — an elegant idea, with relatively high resource cost.

memtensor/memos.pitch: A memory operating system for agents
memtensor/memos.aud: Research or customization at the memory layer
memtensor/memos.note: From a Shanghai Jiao Tong University team, with detailed scheduling and lifecycle management; academic, so you wire it up yourself.

modelcontextprotocol/servers.pitch: The official MCP reference server collection
modelcontextprotocol/servers.aud: Connecting agents to tools and data sources
modelcontextprotocol/servers.note: MCP is now a de facto standard, and this is the official source of example implementations and best practices.

upstash/context7.pitch: An MCP service that feeds agents current documentation
upstash/context7.aud: Anyone tired of stale model knowledge
upstash/context7.note: Pulls versioned docs by library name and works in Cursor or Claude Code right away; indexing depends on a third-party host.

chromedevtools/chrome-devtools-mcp.pitch: Let agents drive Chrome DevTools directly
chromedevtools/chrome-devtools-mcp.aud: Agents that inspect performance, network and console
chromedevtools/chrome-devtools-mcp.note: Officially maintained, adding a runtime view beyond raw DOM manipulation — handy for front-end debugging.

github/github-mcp-server.aud: Agents managing issues, PRs and code search
github/github-mcp-server.note: Official, with permissions bound to the token; GitHub Enterprise needs extra configuration.

composiohq/composio.pitch: A tool hub with 1000+ integrations for agents
composiohq/composio.aud: Connecting agents to the SaaS ecosystem
composiohq/composio.note: A hosted tool marketplace plus managed auth, so you skip OAuth plumbing; the trade-off is dependence on their cloud.

prefecthq/fastmcp.pitch: Write an MCP server in a few lines of Python
prefecthq/fastmcp.note: Decorator style, and currently the least painful way to write MCP services.

a2aproject/a2a.pitch: An agent-to-agent protocol started by Google, now under the Linux Foundation
a2aproject/a2a.aud: Connecting agents across vendors and organizations
a2aproject/a2a.note: Covers the half MCP doesn't: discovery, task delegation and streaming progress between agents; the repo is specification-first, with reference code.

modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.pitch: The official Python SDK for writing MCP servers
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.note: The most authoritative implementation of the protocol itself; pair it with FastMCP for convenience. Protocol only — no agent logic.

mcp-use/mcp-use.pitch: A full-stack MCP framework for MCP apps and servers
mcp-use/mcp-use.aud: Building an MCP app with a UI
mcp-use/mcp-use.note: Bundles an MCP server and a front end into one project, good for interactive tools; public examples are still few.

langfuse/langfuse.pitch: A veteran platform for agent observability and evaluation
langfuse/langfuse.aud: Putting traces and evals on an agent
langfuse/langfuse.note: Self-hosting friendly, with traces, datasets and scoring in one place; many features, so expect some ramp-up.

promptfoo/promptfoo.pitch: Write prompt, agent and RAG tests as config and run them in CI
promptfoo/promptfoo.aud: Teams that want evals in CI
promptfoo/promptfoo.note: Declarative YAML assertions plus red-team scanning, easier than hand-written regression scripts; it is a test framework rather than an observability platform — complementary to Langfuse.

confident-ai/deepeval.pitch: An evaluation framework for unit-testing LLMs and agents
confident-ai/deepeval.note: pytest style with common metrics built in; complex multi-turn scenarios need your own evaluators.

arize-ai/phoenix.aud: Comparing RAG and agent tuning runs
arize-ai/phoenix.note: Start it locally to inspect traces and experiment comparisons; the cloud edition has more.

agentops-ai/agentops.pitch: An agent monitoring SDK you add in a few lines
agentops-ai/agentops.note: The fastest to integrate, less deep than Langfuse; releases have slowed over the past six months.

ukgovernmentbeis/inspect_ai.pitch: The UK AI Safety Institute's evaluation framework
ukgovernmentbeis/inspect_ai.note: Evaluation as versioned task sets, with a sandbox and full logs — common in government and compliance work; less convenient than commercial platforms, but reproducible.

verl-project/verl.pitch: The mainstream foundation for agentic RL training (HybridFlow)
verl-project/verl.aud: Algorithm teams training their own agent policies
verl-project/verl.note: A single-controller, multi-role parallel RL post-training framework; most agentic RL reproductions start here, and the barrier is distributed training rather than the API.

openpipe/art.pitch: An agent RL trainer that turns multi-step tasks into training samples
openpipe/art.aud: Replacing a fixed pipeline with a cheap small model
openpipe/art.note: GRPO plus a trainable tool-calling loop, aimed at matching big models on narrow tasks with small models plus RL; the real cost is building data, not training.

thudm/slime.note: RL for very long trajectories and multi-turn tool calls: rollout on SGLang, training on Megatron; the docs read like a paper, so be ready to read code.

openenv/openenv.pitch: An environment interface standard for RL post-training
openenv/openenv.note: Abstracts environments behind a uniform reset/step/reward interface so training code doesn't change when environments do; very early, with no ecosystem yet.

primeintellect-ai/prime-rl.pitch: An agentic RL stack on decentralized compute
primeintellect-ai/prime-rl.aud: Pooling compute across machines to train agents
primeintellect-ai/prime-rl.note: Asynchronous RL with distributed rollout, aimed at bringing idle compute into training; operational complexity is well above single-machine setups.

e2b-dev/e2b.pitch: A secure cloud sandbox for agents
e2b-dev/e2b.note: Firecracker microVM isolation; a hard requirement for the infrastructure behind coding agents.

mattpocock/skills.pitch: Agree on what you're building before you write code
mattpocock/skills.note: Small composable skills, headlined by /grill-me: the agent asks one question at a time until every design branch is unambiguous. The author argues explicitly against big frameworks governing the process — control stays with the human.

obra/superpowers.pitch: A full set of engineering discipline for coding agents
obra/superpowers.aud: Agents that should deliver through a fixed process
obra/superpowers.note: Fifteen skills in a fixed order: brainstorm, plan, isolate with a worktree, TDD, sub-agent execution, per-task review, wrap-up. The docs state this is mandatory, not advisory.

addyosmani/agent-skills.pitch: The classic SDLC split into six commands
addyosmani/agent-skills.aud: Teams going to production that need quality gates
addyosmani/agent-skills.note: From /spec to /ship, covering define, plan, build, verify, review and release, with about 25 skills and four review personas; every skill ships an 'excuses table' that pre-rebuts lines like 'too simple to test'.

backnotprop/pstack.pitch: Prove it actually runs before calling it done
backnotprop/pstack.aud: Hard-to-reproduce bugs, data migrations, overnight autonomous runs
backnotprop/pstack.note: A mirror of Lauren Tan's (Cursor) workflow, upstream at cursor/plugins; /poteto-mode picks from 22 playbooks with no planning skill, weighting reproduction, forensics and multi-model review.

datawhalechina/hello-agents.pitch: Build an agent from scratch, in Chinese
datawhalechina/hello-agents.aud: People who want the principles before the tooling
datawhalechina/hello-agents.note: Companion code for the book: from the ReAct loop to multi-agent systems and training, every chapter runnable and clearly explained in Chinese.

microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners.aud: Anyone who wants a path that doesn't get lost
microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners.note: Microsoft's 18 lessons, from tool calling to multi-agent systems and production; each has a notebook and exercises. In English, and runnable.

shareai-lab/learn-claude-code.pitch: Write a mini Claude Code yourself
shareai-lab/learn-claude-code.note: The core takeaway is that Bash is enough: a very small reimplementation of the harness's tool loop, so the real code no longer feels like a maze.

hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code.pitch: A resource list for the Claude Code ecosystem
hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code.aud: People who already use it and want ready-made configs
hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code.note: Commands, hooks, workflows and plugins by category, community-submitted and updated almost daily — an inspiration library, not a tutorial.

patchy631/ai-engineering-hub.pitch: Hands-on notebooks from RAG to agents
patchy631/ai-engineering-hub.aud: Readers who can read code and want to run it
patchy631/ai-engineering-hub.note: An engineering-leaning tutorial collection that follows new frameworks (RAG, multi-agent, local deployment); complete code, terse explanation.

datawhalechina/llm-universe.pitch: The first course in LLM application development
datawhalechina/llm-universe.aud: Anyone who hasn't built an LLM app yet
datawhalechina/llm-universe.note: A beginner course covering API calls, prompts, RAG and evaluation — the foundation before agents.

nirdiamant/agents-towards-production.pitch: What a demo needs before it can ship
nirdiamant/agents-towards-production.aud: Demos that work until they hit production
nirdiamant/agents-towards-production.note: Breaks productionization into topics — observability, evaluation, memory, deployment, cost — each with a runnable notebook, focused on architecture decisions.

adongwanai/agentguide.pitch: A systematic roadmap for agent development, in Chinese
adongwanai/agentguide.aud: Anyone who wants a map to follow
adongwanai/agentguide.note: A long Chinese piece covering harness design, context engineering, RAG and MCP, with clear opinions — good as a spine to read alongside code.

wangrongsheng/awesome-llm-resources.pitch: A master index of Chinese LLM resources
wangrongsheng/awesome-llm-resources.note: Organized by multimodal, agents, coding assistance and training/inference, with Chinese annotations; the widest coverage, with uneven quality.

liyupi/ai-guide.pitch: A big Chinese catalog of AI tools and playbooks
liyupi/ai-guide.aud: Newcomers who want to play first
liyupi/ai-guide.note: A resource collection plus a vibe-coding intro, covering tool selection, prompts and deployment; plenty of screenshots and steps, limited depth.

wethinkin/aigc-interview-book.pitch: An interview question bank for AIGC and agent roles
wethinkin/aigc-interview-book.aud: Preparing a resume or an interview
wethinkin/aigc-interview-book.note: Chapters on AIGC, LLMs, agents and embodied AI, with answers — also usable as a checklist for finding gaps.

windy3f3f3f3f/how-claude-code-works.pitch: Take Claude Code apart to see how it works
windy3f3f3f3f/how-claude-code-works.aud: People past the tutorials who want engineering detail
windy3f3f3f3f/how-claude-code-works.note: Walks through architecture, the agent loop, context management and the tool system layer by layer, in Chinese; reading it makes similar products much faster to grasp. Updates are slow.
